key_insight: Self-powered microsystems need not just better harvesters, but tightly co-designed materials, power management, and storage to overcome the battery bottleneck.
engineering_relevance: For IoT and wearable systems, the practical challenge is integrating diverse ambient-energy sources with ultra-low-voltage PMICs and durable storage for reliable field operation.
method: Review key harvester classes: TENGs, piezoelectric/pyroelectric devices, indoor PV, and RF rectennas
Compare hybrid multi-source integration strategies and system-level power management constraints
Highlight emerging advances such as liquid-solid TENGs, nonlinear piezo oscillators, and metamaterial RF harvesting
evidence_signal: The abstract cites specific reported gains, including over 300% broader bandwidth for nonlinear piezoelectric oscillators and improved RF harvesting through multiband/broadband metamaterial architectures.
watch_item: Many promising harvesting and storage approaches still face cold-start, impedance-matching, and real-world degradation issues that can limit deployment.
paper_title: Energy Harvesting for Self-Powered Microsystems: A Critical Review of Materials, Power Management, and System Integration
